questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: First, signal and check traffic. Then stop parallel to the car directly in front of your parking space. After this, turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: It is illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles may share a lane, but cars cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark public recreation areas and historical sites. These signs help you find these places when traveling.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to red.
Do not drive in this lane.
You may only turn left in this lane.
You may drive normally in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive normally in this lane.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A green arrow means the lane is open and you can drive normally.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look, and go if no traffic is coming.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text saying 'No Passing Zone.'

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be treated as:

options.text: Safe, since trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you. This lets you see cars coming your way.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should usually:

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to the same speed as the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: If a vehicle with high beams is coming toward you, look toward the ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right side
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming vehicle has high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay in your lane until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and be careful. Look both ways for traffic before entering.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge that angles toward the left means:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will have to turn left soon.
The road is getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line marks the edge of the road. When the line angles toward the center, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads:

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Leave less space between you and the car ahead.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: You must yield to other drivers:

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When they are on a road to your left and you arrive at an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when you enter from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always drive carefully near cyclists.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic is moving in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic is moving in opposite directions and you can pass when it is safe.
Traffic is moving in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic is moving in the same direction and you can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in the same direction and you can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When the accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep going even when you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition by moving the switch just enough to stop the engine—not so far that it locks the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and pull off the road to a safe spot.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors.
Turn up the car radio to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always walk to the back of your vehicle before getting in to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: When an oncoming car has bright headlights that blind you, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
They do not need more room to turn than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Avoid these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Road hazard warning.
Interstate route sign.
School crossing sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road hazard warning.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow. In work areas, they may be orange. These signs warn you of hazards ahead or areas where special rules apply.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with no traffic light or stop sign?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Yield to everyone else.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield by taking your foot off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway begins.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road gets wider ahead.
Right lane ends soon.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.
Left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if your car with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to lose grip on a slippery road?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal down hard.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Tap the brakes lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal down hard.
questions.explanation: If your Anti-Lock Braking System car loses traction, press hard on the brake and keep holding it while steering to safety. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Releasing the brake or pumping it yourself will turn off the ABS.
